name: refuse-checks-as-a-label
why: `checks: [...]` as a statement of its own is a JavaScript label: legal, evaluated, discarded. A Haiku 5.5 field run wrote the request's checks that way before `return plate;` and the host built the plate with no checks and said nothing. Every runner now asks the engine whether the script carries such a label — the script wrapped in a block labelled `checks` compiles unless it does — and refuses it naming the line and the fix.

message_contains: `checks:` at line 8 is a JavaScript label
